The best counterweight is institutional pushback by the Election Commission and Supreme Court, which suggests checks still existed, but not that Modi voluntarily respected them.","evidence":[{"title":"India top court scraps opaque election funding system, calls it ‘unconstitutional’","publisher":"Reuters via ThePrint","date":"2024-02-15","url":"https://theprint.in/india/india-top-court-scraps-opaque-election-funding-system-calls-it-unconstitutional/1967048/","summary":"The Supreme Court struck down the electoral bonds system, which Modi’s government introduced in 2017 and which let donors give unlimited anonymous money; Reuters says the BJP was the largest beneficiary. This is strong evidence of an electoral-finance structure that advantaged the ruling party and was later judged unconstitutional.","question_ids":["4B.2"]},{"title":"India’s top court puts on hold unit for fact-checking online content about govt","publisher":"Reuters via ThePrint","date":"2024-03-21","url":"https://theprint.in/india/india-top-court-puts-on-hold-unit-for-fact-checking-online-content-about-govt/2009612/","summary":"The government had created a fact-checking unit with power to label online content about central-government business as false or misleading; the Supreme Court stayed it over constitutional concerns. This is direct evidence of an attempted government mechanism to police online information about itself, which would have helped entrench the ruling side.","question_ids":["4B.2"]},{"title":"Election Commission tells government to stop sending ‘Viksit Bharat’ messages on WhatsApp","publisher":"Election Commission of India via Hindustan Times","date":"2024-03-21","url":"https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/election-commission-to-it-ministry-stop-sending-viksit-bharat-messages-on-whatsapp-101711006490551.html","summary":"The Election Commission ordered the ministry to halt government-branded WhatsApp messages because the Model Code of Conduct was in force and complaints said the messages were still reaching voters. This is evidence that public communication channels were being used in a campaign-sensitive way and that the EC had to intervene to stop it.","question_ids":["4B.2"]},{"title":"India’s poll panel orders Modi’s BJP, opposition Congress to show restraint in campaign","publisher":"Reuters via ThePrint","date":"2024-05-22","url":"https://theprint.in/india/indias-poll-panel-orders-modis-bjp-opposition-congress-to-show-restraint-in-campaign/2096809/","summary":"Reuters reported the Election Commission found both parties’ defenses “not tenable” and told BJP campaigners to refrain from communal campaigning after complaints about divisive speech, including Modi’s comments on Muslims. This is direct evidence that Modi’s campaign violated election norms closely enough to trigger formal censure.","question_ids":["4B.2","2B.6"]},{"title":"India BJP’s election videos targeting Muslims and opposition spark outrage","publisher":"Reuters via ThePrint","date":"2024-05-06","url":"https://theprint.in/india/india-bjps-election-videos-targeting-muslims-and-opposition-spark-outrage/2072545/","summary":"The BJP circulated animated campaign videos targeting Muslims and Congress; the opposition complained to the Election Commission that they promoted enmity and provoked rioting. This is evidence of using media content to polarize voters and push communal advantage rather than keeping the contest neutral.","question_ids":["4B.2","2B.6"]},{"title":"India: Hate Speech Fueled Modi’s Election Campaign","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-08-14","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/14/india-hate-speech-fueled-modis-election-campaign","summary":"HRW says Modi’s 2024 campaign frequently used hate speech against Muslims and other minorities and that authorities failed to respond adequately to the violations. That strongly undercuts the claim that he refrained from using rule-bending or divisive tactics to entrench himself.","question_ids":["4B.2","2B.6","3B.3"]},{"title":"India’s General Elections, Technology, and Human Rights Questions and Answers","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-04-08","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/08/india-technology-use-shouldnt-undermine-free-fair-elections","summary":"HRW warned that Indian authorities controlled the digital ecosystem, had a history of using internet shutdowns and platform pressure against critics, and that misuse of government-held personal data could tilt the playing field toward the ruling party. This is broader structural evidence that the incumbent state had tools and incentives to skew the election environment.","question_ids":["4B.2","4B.1"]},{"title":"Indian PM Modi says he does not oppose Islam, Muslims as election campaign heats up","publisher":"Reuters via ThePrint","date":"2024-05-07","url":"https://theprint.in/india/indian-pm-modi-says-he-does-not-oppose-islam-muslims-as-election-campaign-heats-up/2072917/","summary":"Modi denied targeting Muslims and said he would not do “Hindu-Muslim” politics. This is weak counterevidence only because it is a self-serving denial, not an independent sign that the campaign was actually clean.","question_ids":["4B.2","2B.6"]},{"title":"India’s Modi denies stoking divisions to win election, files nomination","publisher":"Reuters via ThePrint","date":"2024-05-14","url":"https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-denies-stoking-divisions-to-win-election-files-nomination/2084849/","summary":"Modi again denied stoking communal division. This is again only weak counterevidence; the contemporaneous reporting and EC complaints still point the other way.","question_ids":["4B.2","2B.6"]}]}
